name: level1-lose-ecology
description:
Level 1 losing scenario: a massive blast with max krackle triggers ecology score collapse and, after a sustained 150-tick zero streak, the government shutdown that actually ends the level (ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS, EcologicalDisaster.ts). Rebuilt again for issue #554 (`charge hole:*` now queues one real, worker-performed `charge_hole` action per hole instead of writing charges instantly, mirroring #553's `drill_hole`): the file's own prior design (tuned for instant charging) blasted right after drilling finished, at tick 230, while wellBeing was still a comfortably positive 51 -- giving ecological_shutdown's 150-tick countdown a huge head start over worker_revolt's independent, wellBeing-driven one. With charging now taking real time, that head start is gone: landing all 49 queued charge_hole orders with only the original 4-crew (who also drilled) took ~305 ticks, during which the original static 15-employee filler cushion -- hired once, up front, and never touched again -- had already been idling since tick 0 and crashed to 0 wellBeing on its own clock, sustaining the 120-tick streak REVOLT_TICKS needs well before the delayed blast could even start ecology's own countdown. worker_revolt won every time.

The key mechanic this file leans on, confirmed by direct probe: once a score clamps to exactly 0, it stays there completely unassisted -- ScoreManager.ts's applyDecay only pulls a score that is strictly between 0 and 100 back toward the neutral 50 (its own `value > 0` check excludes exactly 0), and nothing on this site (no building anywhere in BuildingDefs.ts carries an `ecology` scoreEffect, and the tick loop's own maxRecentVibration input is hardcoded to 0, events.ts) ever pushes ecology back up from there. This is symmetric for wellBeing too (same applyDecay, same `value > 0` exclusion) -- which is exactly the lever this redesign uses: get wellBeing to cross zero AFTER the blast countdown has enough of a head start, rather than racing a wellBeing clock that started ticking at tick 0 and never stopped.

This redesign's fix has two parts, both scenario-JSON-only (no core change):

(1) The 15-employee filler cushion is hired right AFTER drilling finishes (tick 230) instead of before it, so its own idle-decay clock starts fresh at tick 230 instead of tick 0. Confirmed by direct probe: with the original 4-crew drilling alone (no filler dilution at all, since none exist yet), wellBeing crashes to 0 by tick ~130 and sits there through the rest of drilling (with one brief, deterministic recovery blip around tick 170 from the crew's own scheduled break-need rest, back down by tick 180) -- but the instant a FRESH cushion is hired at tick 230, the composite average climbs back out, peaking around wellBeing 66 near tick 370 before beginning its own slow decline. That climb is only possible because the OLD cushion's damage (crashed since tick 0) is never inherited by the new one -- a fresh employee's `morale` starts at 60 (Employee.ts), not wherever the old cushion's had decayed to.

(2) 30 temporary 'blaster'-role employees are hired at the same moment (also after drilling, before charging) purely to land the 49 queued charge_hole orders in parallel -- ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION grants 'blasting' immediately at hire, and charge_hole's requiredVehicleRole is null, so no drill_rig purchase is needed for them. This cuts the charging phase from ~305 ticks (4 workers) to ~118 ticks (34 workers), landing blast at tick 348 instead of 535. They are never fired -- an earlier attempt at this exact fix tried hiring a similar temporary crew and firing them again before the blast, which hit two problems worth recording here: `employee fire` refuses a roster member who unionized while employed (`rng.chance(0.3)` at hire time, Employee.ts) -- with 20-45 temp hires, several always come up unionized and can't be dismissed, so the exact death toll became unpredictable -- and hiring at that volume also shifts the RNG-gated event-selection timer (`actionCountSinceEvent`, EventSystem.ts, incremented by every non-meta console command) enough that a normally-late random political/economic event can land inside the post-blast zero-ecology window and, if its auto-chosen option carries a positive `ecology` scoreDelta (e.g. politics_ev_mandate's default option, `{ecology: 18}`), break the sustained-zero streak outright. This redesign sidesteps both: the temp blasters are never fired (no unionization check to fail), and they die in the very blast they helped charge -- deathCount goes 0->34 (4 original crew + 30 temp blasters), while the fresh, never-tasked 15-employee filler cushion, standing at the depot the whole time, survives to carry wellBeing through the post-blast countdown.

Timing, confirmed by direct probe (fully deterministic given the fixed seed and this exact command sequence -- no RNG in any of the formulas this race depends on): drilling ends at tick 230 (unchanged from every prior version of this file -- always 4 crew, always ~230 ticks for 49 holes at 2m spacing). Hiring the fresh filler + 30 temp blasters is instantaneous (hiring costs no ticks). Charging all 49 holes with 34 blasting-qualified workers takes 118 ticks, landing blast at tick 348. The blast clamps ecology to exactly 0 and kills all 34 present (deathCount 34); ecological_shutdown's 150-tick countdown then runs uninterrupted (nothing on this site ever pushes ecology back up), firing at tick 498. Meanwhile the fresh filler cushion's own wellBeing, no longer dragged down by the temp blasters' fast working-rate need drain once they die in the blast, climbs for a while before resuming its own decline, crossing back to 0 around tick 448 -- REVOLT_TICKS=120 after that is ~568, a comfortable 70-tick margin behind shutdown's tick 498. events.ts's tick loop only ever sets levelEndReason on the FIRST condition to trip a given tick (bankruptcy, then ecological shutdown, then arrest, then revolt, each gated by `if (!state.levelEnded)`) -- once shutdown locks it in at tick 498, nothing later (including revolt's own counter, which is still climbing) can overwrite it.

steps.description: staffed:true does NOT auto-assign a driver -- crews the free drill_rig (vehicle #1) with employee #1, the only qualified driller already on the roster.

Only vehicle #1 (drill_rig) is used this round -- the staffed roster's debris_hauler/rock_digger/rock_fragmenter would otherwise sit parked in the drill site's path: NavGrid pathing has no notion of "move aside", so a vehicle idling on a cell a drilling driller's route crosses blocks that route forever (isCellOccupiedByOtherVehicle, EntityMovementTick.ts) -- confirmed by direct probe, drilling stalls at a handful of holes indefinitely with these left in place, regardless of crew size.

Hiring a driller only grants the role's starting `blasting` qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION, Employee.ts) -- the drill_rig licence needed before any drill_hole action can be assigned to them comes from here. No UI equivalent: the player-facing path is `employee train` at a driving_center.

The assign row's own <select> (fleetDetailSections.ts's makeAssignRow) must be explicitly set to this employee before clicking Assign -- Assign reads whichever employee the <select> currently shows, which defaults to the first eligible (alive, licensed, not-yet-driving) one in roster order, not whichever employee this step names.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:7 cols:7 spacing:2 depth:6 diameter:0.089 start:5,5
steps.description: One decrement click on the strip's own spacing stepper (data-field="spacing", DEFAULT_SPACING_M=3 -> 2, Drill.ts) before dragging the SAME (5,5)-(17,17) box round1 always used: 7x7 holes at 2m spacing spans exactly the 12m this drag already covers (round((17-5)/2)+1=7), the same span 5x5 holes at the old 3m spacing covered (round(12/3)+1=5). Tight 2m spacing is not cosmetic -- confirmed by direct probe, it is what keeps 4 parallel crews finishing all 49 holes in ~230 ticks instead of ~600+: closer holes mean shorter drives between them, which is most of the difference between a crew that finishes with wellBeing still above 50 and one that has already crashed to 0 and cannot recover before the blast.

Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently misses events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s (#475), leaving them pending so later ticks halt and the run diverges while still passing command mode.

230 ticks (23 x tick 10, deterministic given the fixed seed and this exact command sequence) is enough for the 4 parallel driller+drill_rig crews to finish all 49 holes -- confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism (holeCount 49, wellBeing 51.16 both times).

#554 recalibration: moved here (right after drilling, instead of before it) so the filler cushion's own idle-decay clock starts at tick 230, not tick 0 -- see this file's own top-level description for why: with only the original 4-crew drilling first (no filler dilution at all), wellBeing already crashes to 0 by tick ~130 and sits there through the rest of drilling, but a FRESH 15-employee cushion hired the instant drilling ends climbs back out of that hole (peaking ~66 by tick ~370) instead of continuing to decay from a roster that had already been idling since tick 0 -- exactly the margin needed against REVOLT_TICKS=120 once real charging time (#554) pushes blast hundreds of ticks later than the old instant-charge design ever had to survive.

Temporary charging crew (30x 'blaster' role -- ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION grants 'blasting' immediately, no drill_rig/vehicle needed since charge_hole's requiredVehicleRole is null): with only the original 4 driller crew able to charge, landing all 49 queued charge_hole orders took ~305 ticks serially/4-wide, long enough that even the fresh filler cushion above crashes and resolves worker_revolt before the delayed blast ever starts ecological_shutdown's own countdown. 30 more parallel charging hands land the same 49 holes in ~120 ticks instead. They are never fired -- they charge, then stand exactly where the blast needs everyone to stand for the catastrophe this file is testing, and die alongside the original 4 crew (deathCount 34) rather than surviving to dilute (or being routed through a firing dance that trips on random unionization, #554 finding). Once they're gone, only the still-fresh filler cushion remains to carry wellBeing through the post-blast countdown.

Blast panel was last closed by the employee-hiring loop above (last opened #bs-toolbar [data-panel="employees"] at step 71) -- clicking #bs-blast-panel [data-step="2"] directly on a hidden panel (display:none on the whole panel root, BlastWorkshop.ts) hits a zero-size element, confirmed by real interaction-mode CI. Reopen the Blast panel via its toolbar tab first, same as step 23 above.

#554/#590 finding: charging 49 holes with a 34-strong temporary blaster crew is real, worker-performed work that takes long enough (118 ticks) for a spontaneous event to plausibly fire mid-wait -- a single long `waitUntil` has no way to resolve one in interaction mode (its real, isPaused-gated clock halts exactly as it would for a real player, per interaction-executor.ts's own waitUntil doc comment), so the drain stalls forever at whatever count was ordered when the event hit. Command mode's own waitUntil auto-resolves silently and never showed this. Chunked here into the same tick-N/event-choose-0 pattern already used for this file's own drilling wait above, which does resolve mid-wait events in both modes. Sized to exactly 118 ticks total (matching the original single waitUntil's own measured figure, confirmed by direct probe) -- this file's blast-to-shutdown timing race is exact-tick-sensitive (see this file's own top-level description and the final step's tickCount:498 assertion), so no padding is added here: an extra tick would shift every absolute tick number after it.

The catastrophic blast -- this file's whole point. ~90m throw radius is unavoidable on this map for anyone standing at the drill site, so all 34 present there die (deathCount 0->34: the original 4-crew (employees #1, #6, #7, #8) plus the 30 temporary 'blaster' hires that landed the charges above); the 15 filler cushion, hired right after drilling and never given a task, stay at the depot and survive. Krackle vibration cuts ecology sharply in one blast, deterministically (no RNG in the blast->ecology formula, ScoreManager.ts's recordVibration) -- 49 holes at this spacing/charge produce enough projections (confirmed by direct probe) to clamp ecology to exactly 0, not merely low. That exact-0 clamp is what starts the government's countdown: applyDecay (ScoreManager.ts) only nudges a score that is strictly between 0 and 100 back toward 50 -- at exactly 0 (`value > 0` excludes it) it does nothing, and with no building anywhere on this site touching the ecology score and maxRecentVibration hardcoded to 0 in the tick loop (events.ts), nothing else ever will either. Ecology stays pinned at exactly 0 from this tick on, unassisted, for the full ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 streak below -- one sufficiently large blast is enough; no second round is needed.

150 more ticks (15 x tick 10) after the blast -- ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS (EcologicalDisaster.ts). Ecology, pinned at exactly 0 since the blast above, reaches the sustained streak here; the government shutdown fires on the very last of these ticks (confirmed by direct probe, run twice for determinism: tick 380 both times). wellBeing recovers only partway (the surviving 15 filler's own morale has also been draining on pure idle-gauge decay since tick 0 -- REVOLT_TICKS=120 is close enough behind ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 that this file's pacing is the whole point: worker_revolt's own ticksAtZero streak reaches only ~97 of the 120 it needs by the time shutdown locks the outcome in -- events.ts's tick loop sets levelEndReason on the FIRST condition to trip a given tick (bankruptcy, then ecological shutdown, then arrest, then revolt, each gated by `if (!state.levelEnded)`), so once shutdown claims it here, revolt's own later-arriving streak can never overwrite it.

expect.note: Final state confirms the government shutdown -- fired for real exactly ECOLOGICAL_SHUTDOWN_TICKS=150 after the single blast above, at tick 498 (blast now lands at tick 348: drilling still ends at 230 as always, and landing all 49 charge_hole orders with the 30-strong temporary blaster crew above takes ~118 ticks, #554: charging is real work now). worker_revolt's own, independently-running wellBeing streak crosses zero around tick 448 (the fresh 15-employee filler cushion, hired right after drilling instead of before it, climbs back toward positive wellBeing once the temporary blaster crew dies and stops dragging the average down, then decays back to 0 on its own clock) -- REVOLT_TICKS=120 after that is ~568, well after shutdown already claims levelEndReason at 498, confirmed by direct probe. cash stays comfortably positive throughout (never within remote reach of bankruptcy) -- the $5,000,000 starting cash in this file's own campaign-start command is headroom for direct, repeatable probing of the ecology/wellBeing pacing, not a requirement of the mechanic itself.
